question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186087824/plots/shift-stretch-v5/37d3d6ef86dad6029611d262d295aeefe5569cf93bf29accda7b0e12620c8365.png)

The graph above shows $y=k({3}^{x})+c.$ Determine the values of $k$ and $c$ and find the equation of the curve.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The horizontal asymptote of the curve $y=k({3}^{x})+c$ is $y=c.$ In the graph above, the horizontal asymptote is $y=0.75,$ so $c=0.75.$

Therefore, our function takes the form

$$
y=k({3}^{x})+0.75.
$$

We can solve for $k$ by finding a point on the graph and substituting for $x$ and $y.$ Reading the calibrated grid, the marked point on the graph is $(0,5),$ so we substitute $x=0$ and $y=5$ into the function and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =k({3}^{x})+0.75 \\ 5 & =k({3}^{0})+0.75 \\ 5 & =k(1)+0.75 \\ 5 & =k+0.75 \\ 4.25 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the curve is $y=4.25({3}^{x})+0.75.$
